tagline: A mountain village on the slopes of the Karkas range, Isfahan province, Iran

distances.source: Kojaro gives both '15 km east' and 'Meymeh borders on the west'

location.route: From the Shahin Shahr to Meymeh road, turn off about 50 km north of Shahin Shahr at Dehlor, then pass Bidshak. Soh is at the end of the road. There is no bus terminal or railway station in the village.

populationNote: Kojaro says about 1,000 people are in the village in spring and summer (seasonal residents for 7 to 8 months). This is not a census figure.

facts.label: Language
facts.value: Persian, with a local dialect (not yet documented)

history.text: Said to be more than 2,000 years old. Evidence cited: castles with Gabri (Zoroastrian-era) names, the Nachaft castle, the Qal'eh Miyan, millstones and the ruins of a fire temple. FA Wikipedia states that no documents support the age.
The name is said to come from 'sohi' or 'sahi', meaning tall or high, because the village sits on the slopes of the Karkas (کرکس) mountains.
The caravan road made the village a trading and resting point until the middle of the Qajar era. Surviving buildings date from the Safavid and Qajar periods.
Until 1996 (1375) the village belonged to Natanz County, then was separated.

landmarks.name: Soh Caravanserai
landmarks.text: A stone inscription on the portal dates it to 1223 AH (1808 CE), in the reign of Fath-Ali Shah Qajar, with the builder named as Abolqasem Esfahani. About 3,000 m², four iwans and 20 rooms around a courtyard. National monument no. 7641 (registered 17 Esfand 1381). Restored 1395 to 1400 with local donations.

landmarks.name: Imamzadeh Yusuf
landmarks.text: Shrine in the upper village, about 400 years old, with a 16 m dome in turquoise tile. Said to be the resting place of Yusuf, son of Imam Hadi.

landmarks.name: Imamzadeh Golileh
landmarks.text: Turquoise-domed shrine in the lower village, at its centre.

landmarks.name: The old bath
landmarks.text: A Qajar-era bath about 200 years old. Of the upper and lower baths, one survives, restored with local help.

landmarks.name: Kadkhoda house
landmarks.text: Home of the village headman, Mirza Bahram Safavi.

landmarks.name: Other historic places
landmarks.text: Nav Bridge (پل نواب), the Imamzadeh mill and two other mills, the old telegraph house, a dovecote tower, Mirza Jafar's house, a brick kiln and a small zurkhaneh (traditional gym).

landmarks.name: More historic places
landmarks.text: Abbasi caravanserai at Aqa Kamal Pain (on the access road), a mosque about 200 years old beside the bath, four forts (Bala, Pain, Miyan, Chal), a Farangi mansion, the covered passage (sabat) in the upper-castle alley and Kandeh Baghestan.

places: Kuh-e Char and Kuh-e Baghal Siyah mountains
A waterfall, Sarkarriz, Gol Parde Haz, Nachaft, Zir-Pol

livelihood.summary: About 86% of residents worked in agriculture in a survey from 2007 to 2008: crops 56%, livestock 27%, beekeeping 2.4%, poultry 0.8%. Homes are spread out, far from the fields and orchards. Water comes mainly from surface streams. In wetter years lentils, chickpeas, beans and saffron are also mentioned (FA Wikipedia).
livelihood.apples: The apples are described as among the best in Isfahan province, and about 30% of the village's economic capacity is apple growing.
crafts: Hand-woven carpets in the Joshaqani style, sold in Isfahan and Tehran

traditions.text: On Tasua, during Muharram, the village carries a palm-shaped standard (nakhl-gardani). It is decorated in the morning at Imamzadeh Yusuf, carried to Imamzadeh Golileh, and returned after the Ashura noon mourning. Other rituals include alam-gardani, ammar-gardani, taziyeh and nowheh chanting. Kojaro says these mourning rituals are about 200 years old and were listed in Iran's national intangible heritage (no. 1207) on 5 Mordad 1395. The amari (a small wooden bier-frame, kept by one family) is carried on the 8th; seven standards (five coloured, two black) lead the palm on Tasua; chest-beating and dirges start on the first night (Mehr News, single source). Local foods: kalleh-joosh, kashk-e mama, tanoori abgoosht, golmisheh, shami, semnu.

people.note: Only people with a source. Behzad Ghaderi, Lotfollah Khadem Sohi, Yousef Bakhshizadeh Sohi, Farshid Navabi Sohi and Seyed Farhad Sohi appear on FA Wikipedia only; no second source was found, and one report says FA Wikipedia does not even link Ghaderi to Soh, so they are not published.

list.name: Seyed Ali Safavi Sohi
list.text: Born 29 July 1940; commanded the 293rd tank battalion; killed by shrapnel 2 August 1983 (place differs by source: Fakkeh or Jangal-e Amqar). Father Seyed Musa Safavi. A Tehran bridge carries his name. Whether he is from this Soh is medium confidence (FA Wikipedia, Khabar Foori Mar 2021).

list.name: Mirza Bahram Safavi
list.text: Village headman; his house is a historic site (Kojaro).

list.name: Abolqasem Esfahani
list.text: Builder named on the caravanserai inscription (Kojaro).

Seasonal population: Kojaro says ~1,000 in spring/summer, Gardeshnama says up to 5,000 (Nowruz, Muharram, summer).
Distance to Meymeh/Shahin Shahr: Kojaro says 15 km, 65 km and 75 km in different places.

Intangible heritage no. 1207 (Kojaro): not confirmed elsewhere.
Saray-e Moallem eco-lodge is in Tarq Rud (Natanz County), not near Soh.
